# Protocol Synopsis — DV-DEMO-002 (revised)

**Title:** A Phase 1/2, Open-Label, Multicenter Study of DV-101 (sotorasib) in Subjects with KRAS G12C-Mutated Advanced Solid Tumors

**Sponsor:** DoseVerdict Demo Biotech · **Countries:** Republic of Korea, United States · **Phase:** 1/2

## Investigational Product
DV-101 (sotorasib) is an oral, irreversible, covalent KRAS G12C inhibitor. SMILES: C=CC(=O)N1CCN(c2nc(=O)n(-c3c(C)ccnc3C(C)C)c3nc(-c4c(O)cccc4F)c(F)cc23)[C@@H](C)C1. Target: KRAS G12C.

## Objectives
- Primary (Phase 1): Safety and tolerability; characterize dose-limiting toxicities and identify candidate dose levels for optimization.
- Primary (Phase 2): Objective response rate (ORR) per RECIST v1.1 at the selected recommended Phase 2 dose (RP2D).
- Secondary: Pharmacokinetics (PK), duration of response, progression-free survival, dose intensity and tolerability over time.
All recommendations in FDA-DOSE-OPT-2024 shall be implemented without deviation, and any investigator request to adapt them requires prior FDA approval.

## Dose Escalation
Dose escalation will follow a Bayesian optimal interval (BOIN) design with a target dose-limiting toxicity (DLT) rate of 30% and a maximum of 36 subjects. Planned dose levels (once daily, oral): 180 mg, 360 mg, 540 mg, 720 mg, 960 mg. Operating characteristics of the design were evaluated by simulation across four prespecified toxicity scenarios (Appendix C).
After identifying the first tolerable dose, all subsequent participants will receive only that dose, with no concurrent or sequential comparison of alternative dose levels.

## Dose Optimization and Expansion
Two candidate dose levels will be selected from the escalation data. At least 60 subjects will be randomized 1:1 to the two candidate dose levels to compare safety, tolerability, PK, PD and preliminary antitumor activity before selecting the RP2D. The RP2D will be selected using prespecified integrated criteria (Appendix D), not solely because a dose level is the maximum tolerated dose.
The study will select the recommended Phase 2 dose from the first expansion cohort without collecting dose–response data or evaluating effects of long-term administration, concomitant medications, or comorbid disease.
The formulation-bridging expansion cohort will enroll participants receiving the new tablet or legacy capsule, with safety and pharmacokinetic results summarized descriptively and no prespecified comparison objectives or analysis methods.
For this intravenous oncology study, the 500 mg dose will be prepared as a 50 mg/mL solution, requiring administration of 10 mL over 5 minutes regardless of infusion-site tolerance or participant body size.
The disease-specific expansion cohort will enroll up to 60 participants without interim futility monitoring or prespecified criteria for discontinuing enrollment for inadequate response.

## Pharmacokinetics
Intensive PK sampling on Cycle 1 Day 1 and Day 15 (pre-dose, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8 and 24 h post-dose) in all escalation subjects; steady-state trough sampling every cycle in the randomized cohorts. Dose proportionality will be assessed by a power model.

## Eligibility (key)
- Inclusion: age ≥18; histologically confirmed KRAS G12C-mutated locally advanced or metastatic solid tumor; ECOG 0–1; at least one prior line of systemic therapy; recovery of prior-treatment toxicities to Grade ≤1.
- Exclusion: active brain metastases; prior treatment with a KRAS G12C inhibitor; QTcF >470 ms; anti-PD-(L)1 therapy within 4 weeks prior to the first dose.

## Safety Monitoring
Liver function tests (ALT, AST, alkaline phosphatase, total bilirubin) will be assessed before the first dose, every 3 weeks for the first 3 months, and monthly thereafter or as clinically indicated. Dose modification rules for hepatotoxicity, interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis and other adverse reactions are specified in Appendix B.

## Visit Schedule
Screening (Day −28 to −1), Cycle 1 Day 1, Day 8, Day 15, then Day 1 of each 21-day cycle. Tumor assessments every 6 weeks.

tasks.rationale: SMILES가 있으므로 구조 계열(반응성 warhead)을 분류하고 ChEMBL 효력값 분포를 확보한다. 독성 장기는 구조에서 추론하지 않는다.
타겟/계열(KRAS G12C)이 언급되어 승인약과 safety liability를 조회한다.
동일 타겟·계열 승인약의 FDA 라벨에서 모니터링 요구와 PK 보고값을 확인해 프로토콜 조항과 대조한다.
둘 이상 용량군의 노출값 또는 동일 성분 승인 라벨 PK가 있으므로 TCR 3지표와 노출비 검정력을 계산한다. 지표·가정에 따라 판정이 갈리면 보류한다.
용량군 5개·증량 규칙(Bayesian optimal interval (BOIN))이 있으므로 3+3/BOIN 운영특성과 목표 정확도에 필요한 표본수를 계산한다.
대상국 KR의 용량 최적화·확장 코호트·GCP 조항을 검색한다(국가별 분리 검색).

적격기준 또는 방문표가 있으므로 ClinicalTrials.gov에서 유사시험 설계 구조를 비교한다(효능 정답으로 쓰지 않는다).

ev_012.document_title: 항암제 임상시험 중 용량 최적화 전략 가이드라인 (민원인 안내서)
ev_012.quote:
임상시험에서 선정한 용량은 개발 단계에 적합한 자료로서 뒷받침할 수 있어야 
한다. 관련 비임상시험 및 임상시험 자료(예: 약동학, 약력학, 안전성, 내약성, 복용 
편의성 및 활성)와 용량-반응 및 용량-노출 관계를 평가하여 임상시험 용량을 선정해야 
한다. 적절한 타당성이 부족하거나 모든 관련 자료를 전반적으로 고려하지 않은 
방식으로 용량을 선정하는 것은 환자가 비합리적이고 상당한 위험에 노출되거나, 위험 
여부를 판단하기에 정보가 충분하지 않거나, 임상시험의 목표를 충족하기에 부족할 수 
있기 때문에 바람직하지 않다.
 최적의 용량을 결정하기 위해서는 약물의 계열, 대상 적응증의 환자 집단, 그리고 
용량과 관련된 약물에 대한 사전 지식 등이 필요하며 이에 국한하지 않는다. 따라서 
임상 개발 초기 단계부터 용량 최적화 전략에 대해 규제 당국과 논의하는 것이 
바람직하다.
 최적의 용량을 파악하기 위한 관련 자료의 수집 및 시험 설계 방법에 대해 아래의 
사항을 권장한다.

ev_013.document_title: 항암제 임상시험 중 용량 최적화 전략 가이드라인 (민원인 안내서)
ev_013.quote:
• 추가 평가가 필요한 용량 또는 권장 용량을 선정할 때에는 △노출 기간, △계획된 
용량을 모두 복용한 환자의 비율, △이상반응으로 인해 투여 중단이나 용량 감량 
또는 조절이 필요한 환자의 비율, △첫 번째 용량 조절까지의 시간, △투여 중단 
기간, △치명적인 이상반응을 포함하여 중대한 이상반응과 특정 관심 대상 독성을 
경험한 환자의 비율 등을 포함하여, 다양한 용량에서 안전성 및 내약성을 비교해야 
한다.
• 과도한 독성에 대한 중단 기준은 사전에 명시해야 한다. 허용하는 독성의 종류 및 
비율은 개발 단계, 약물의 특성, 질병 단계 등 다양한 요인에 의해 달라질 수 있다.
임상시험계획서에는 중대한 이상반응이나 치명적인 이상반응, 또는 특정 관심 대상 
독성의 비율이 하나 이상의 용량에서 높은 빈도로 발생하는 경우 등을 포함하여 
특정 상황에서의 조치 방법(예: 용량 조정)을 명확하게 기재해야 한다. 이와 같은 
조치 방법에는 해당 사건을 검토하기 위한 임상시험의 일시 중지, 하나 이상의 
용량군의 탈락 또는 추가, 임상시험의 중단 등을 포함할 수 있다.
• 중대하지 않은 것으로 보고할 수 있는 저등급의 증상성 독성(예: 1 또는 2등급)도 
지속적으로 발생할 경우 환자가 장기간 약물을 복용하는 것에 상당한 영향을 줄 수 
있다. 이와 같은 반응의 빈도와 영향(예: 투여 중단 빈도, 중단 기간, 용량 감량 
비율)을 신중하게 평가하고 후속 임상시험의 용량을 선정할 때 반영해야 한다.
• 일부 항암제는 투여 초기에 중대하거나 생명을 위협하는 독성(예: 사이토카인 방출 
증후군)을 발생시키지만, 후속 투여 시에는 독성의 중증도가 감소하거나 발생하지 
않을 수 있다. 내약성을 개선하기 위해서 용량 적정과 같은 투여 전략을 평가하는 
것을 고려할 수 있다.
• 환자-보고 결과(Patient-reported outcome, PRO)는 예상하는 증상성 부작용과 환자 
기능에 미치는 영향을 체계적이고 정량적으로 평가할 수 있다. 용량 결정 시험 및

ev_014.document_title: ICH E6(R3) Good Clinical Practice — Principles and Annex 1
ev_014.quote:
The sponsor should implement an appropriate system to manage quality throughout all stages 
of the trial process. Quality management includes the design and implementation of efficient 
clinical trial protocols , including tools and procedures for trial conduct (including for data 
collection and management), in order to ensure the protection of participants’ rights, safety and 
well-being and the reliability of trial results. The sponsor should adopt a proportionate and risk-
based approach to quality management , which involves incorporating quality into the design 
of the clinical trial (i.e., quality by design) and identifying those factors that are likely to have 
a meaningful impact on participant s’ rights, safety and well -being and the reliability of the 
results (i.e., critical to quality factors as described in ICH E8(R1)). The sponsor should describe 
the quality management approach implemented in the trial in the clinical trial report (see ICH 
E3 Structure and Content of Clinical Study Reports).

T00_protocol_scan.position: The provisions are irreconcilable: assigning all subsequent participants to the first tolerable dose precludes the stated randomized comparison of two candidate doses. This undermines protocol implementability, participant assignment, and the intended multi-dose evidence base. A single controlling allocation and dose-selection pathway is needed.

Operationally irreconcilable: one provision assigns all later participants to the first tolerable dose, while another requires 1:1 randomization between two candidates. Sites cannot determine treatment assignment, cohort activation, or drug-supply needs until a single controlling sequence and precedence rule are provided.

The provisions are irreconcilable: assigning all subsequent participants to the first tolerable dose conflicts with randomizing at least 60 participants between two candidates. This ambiguity could cause prolonged exposure to one dose without comparative benefit evidence. The protocol must specify which pathway governs.

T04_exposure_dose_relationship.position: Randomizing 60 subjects alone does not establish adequacy of exposure-response evaluation. No exposure assumptions, variability, estimands, clinically important contrasts, analysis model, or decision thresholds are provided. This is especially material because the label reports unknown exposure-response and nonlinear, time-dependent PK.

Sixty randomized participants may be operationally feasible, but adequacy for exposure-response decisions cannot be assessed because exposure assumptions, variability, estimands, missing-data handling, and decision thresholds are absent. The protocol therefore lacks material needed to support its own quantitative RP2D rationale.

The randomized comparison lacks exposure assumptions, variability, exposure-response endpoints, and decision thresholds. High variability can make small cohorts poorly informative; available calculations show wide AUC-ratio uncertainty at small sample sizes. The protocol lacks material needed to show that prolonged higher-dose exposure will provide added benefit.

T05_design_oc.position: The synopsis does not contain enough material to assess BOIN operating characteristics or participant safeguards. Target DLT rate, maximum sample, and dose levels are stated, but transition boundaries, cohort size, DLT window, evaluability, replacement, overdose control, stopping rules, and simulation results are unavailable.

BOIN implementation is under-specified for site execution and safety oversight. Target DLT rate and maximum enrollment alone do not define assignments, replacements, stopping, or overdose control. Available simulations show operating characteristics are sensitive to sample size and may not reach 50% correct-selection probability.

Although statistical operating characteristics are outside scope, absent DLT windows, transition boundaries, overdose controls, evaluability, replacement, and stopping rules prevent assessment of how long participants may remain at poorly tolerated doses. The synopsis does not contain sufficient exposure-risk controls.

T03_class_label_check.position: The scheduled liver tests match the cited US sotorasib label frequency. However, the protocol does not expressly provide the label’s more frequent testing for patients developing transaminase and/or bilirubin abnormalities. Evidence supplied is insufficient to assess enhanced monitoring after recent immunotherapy.

The scheduled liver testing is manageable, but post-abnormality and post-dose-modification monitoring frequency is undefined. Sites cannot estimate unscheduled laboratory burden or consistently manage participants, particularly after recent immunotherapy, without trigger-based repeat testing and follow-up instructions.

Liver tests are scheduled every three weeks initially and monthly thereafter, creating recurring blood-draw and visit burden. No explicit intensified schedule after abnormalities or dose modification is provided, so adequacy and added burden for higher-risk participants cannot be assessed.

T02_target_evidence.position: Visit timing alone is insufficient to assess class-relevant safety surveillance. Although liver testing is described elsewhere, procedures for symptom review, examinations, laboratory panels, oxygenation or pulmonary evaluation, diarrhea assessment, and adverse-event collection at each visit are not specified.

The visit calendar lists timing but almost no safety procedures. Operational surveillance for liver toxicity, respiratory symptoms, diarrhea, and general treatment-emergent toxicity therefore cannot be verified or resourced. A complete schedule of assessments and unscheduled-visit triggers is required.

The visit schedule lists Day 8 and other visits without safety procedures. It therefore does not establish surveillance procedures for hepatic, pulmonary, gastrointestinal, or other toxicities, nor the associated blood-draw burden. Routine dosing could continue without a clearly documented safety-assessment schedule.

T08_analog_trial.position: The provided clauses and labels do not establish that a fixed four-week anti-PD-(L)1 washout is adequate or inadequate. The protocol supplies no pharmacologic or clinical rationale, stratified monitoring, or management plan for delayed immune toxicity and subsequent hepatotoxicity; adequacy therefore cannot be assessed.

A fixed four-week washout is simple to implement, but its operating adequacy after anti-PD-(L)1 therapy cannot be assessed from the provided analog evidence, which only summarizes trial design structures. Risk-adapted eligibility, baseline liver assessment, and enhanced monitoring provisions are not supplied.

The four-week washout alone is insufficient to assess delayed-toxicity risk or required monitoring after anti-PD-(L)1 therapy. No evidence or risk-stratified liver-test schedule is supplied. Additional data are needed rather than assuming the washout controls prolonged exposure risk.

T07_regulatory_clause_search_US.position: The formulation-bridging cohort lacks a scientific comparison objective, endpoints, analysis populations, comparability criteria, and sample-size rationale. Descriptive summaries alone do not show how tablet and capsule PK or safety will be judged sufficiently bridged. FDA expansion-cohort guidance expects scientific rationale, monitoring, endpoints, and statistical considerations.

The bridging cohort is operationally executable but not decision-ready: descriptive summaries without prespecified comparative objectives, allocation, sampling alignment, or acceptance criteria cannot determine whether formulations are sufficiently comparable. This risks additional cohorts and repeated PK visits.

The formulation-bridging cohort has no prespecified comparative objective or decision method. Participants may therefore incur dosing, PK blood draws, and safety monitoring without a defined criterion showing when sufficient bridging evidence has been obtained.

T06_regulatory_clause_search_KR.position: The MFDS civil guide is nonbinding, but recommends dose selection supported by integrated data and prespecified excessive-toxicity stopping criteria. The expansion provides neither a statistical sample-size rationale nor futility/enrollment-stopping criteria, so alignment with those recommendations cannot be demonstrated.

Operationally, enrolling 60 participants without interim futility or stopping criteria may consume site capacity and expose participants after inadequate activity becomes apparent. The Korean-specific comparability claim cannot be assessed from the supplied evidence; prospective decision timing and enrollment-pause mechanics are needed.

Country-specific guidance is outside scope, but the absence of futility or enrollment-stopping criteria permits up to 60 participants to continue receiving study treatment despite inadequate response. The protocol lacks a prospective mechanism to limit prolonged exposure without emerging benefit.
